member.name: T:Debugger.Program
member.summary: Main entry point for the Debugger module test application.

remarks.para: This program demonstrates the file processing capabilities of the Debugger module by scanning a directory for VHDL files and parsing each one to identify entities and architectures.
The program currently serves as a test harness for the class, which is the core component responsible for bridging VHDL source files with the Interpreter module's data models.

member.name: M:Debugger.Program.Main(System.String[])
member.summary: Application entry point that processes all VHDL files in the "Codes" directory.

remarks.para:
For each VHDL file found in the "Codes" directory:
Creates a new Parser instance with the file path
Calls ParseFile() to identify entity and architecture blocks
Reports the number of entities found in the file

Expected directory structure:
Debugger/ ├── Program.cs ├── Repositories/ │ └── Parser.cs └── Codes/ ├── test1.vhdl ├── test2.vhdl └── ...

member.exception: Thrown if the "Codes" directory does not exist.

member.name: T:Debugger.Repositories.Parser
member.summary: Bridge between VHDL source files and the Interpreter module's data models.

remarks.para: The Parser class is responsible for reading VHDL source files and extracting structural information to create and objects that can be used by the Interpreter module for simulation.

Parsing Algorithm: The parser uses a simple state machine approach with three states:
it=0: Default state - looking for entity or architecture keywords
it=1: Inside entity block - collecting lines until "end" keyword
it=2: Inside architecture block - collecting lines until "end" keyword

item.description: Uses string matching rather than full tokenization for structure detection
The Tokenizer is instantiated but not actively used (reserved for future enhancement)

member.name: F:Debugger.Repositories.Parser._excludedEnds
member.summary: Keywords that should not be treated as end-block markers when they follow end. Without these, lines like end loop; inside a for-loop or end case; inside a process body would prematurely terminate the architecture and feed Synthesize() a truncated chunk.

member.name: M:Debugger.Repositories.Parser.ParseFile
member.summary: Parses the VHDL file content to identify and create Entity and Architecture objects.

item.description: Split file content into lines and normalize whitespace
Iterate through lines using state machine (it variable)
When "entity" keyword found, switch to entity collection mode (it=1)
When "architecture" keyword found, extract entity name and switch to architecture mode (it=2)
Collect lines until appropriate "end" keyword is found
Create Entity or Architecture objects from collected lines

remarks.para: Entity/Architecture Association: The architecture declaration specifies which entity it belongs to using the syntax: architecture ArchName of EntityName is. The parser extracts the entity name (at index 3 after splitting by space) and looks it up in the Entities list.

member.exception: Thrown with message "Entity not found" if an architecture references an entity that was not previously parsed from the file.

member.name: M:Debugger.Repositories.Parser.RunDiagnostics(System.String)
member.summary:
Lightweight source-level validator run after . Emits warning-level diagnostics for common student mistakes:
Statement-ending lines without the expected semicolon.
Mismatched begin / end depth.
Runs character-by-character on the ORIGINAL (not the whitespace-collapsed array used by ParseFile) so the line/column coords it reports still match what the student sees in Monaco.

member.name: M:Debugger.Repositories.Parser.LooksLikeStatement(System.String)
member.summary: Heuristic: does this stripped-and-lower-cased line look like a statement that ought to end with a semicolon? Rules out declarations whose terminators are handled by block parsers (entity/architecture/ process/if/case/when), library imports, and obvious keywords.
